questions.q: What three phases make up the design thinking process?
questions.why: Lesson 1 names the phases and says design thinking considers all three together rather than in sequence.

questions.q: Why does design thinking treat the phases as overlapping?
a: Real projects loop through them more than once
It removes the need for testing
questions.why: Lesson 1 observes that few projects move neatly from one phase to the next and usually revisit each.

questions.q: Which three criteria should guide every step of a project?
questions.why: Lesson 1 uses the Nintendo Wii to show a product that worked well, made business sense and appealed to customers.

questions.q: What does the summary recommend about prototyping?
a: Start as early as possible, even with rough models
Wait until the design is fully polished
Test only after the product launches
questions.why: Lesson 2 says building early reveals limits and opportunities, citing Apple's first mouse made from household items.

questions.q: How should you make a new idea stick with people?
a: Tell stories about how it was made and used
questions.why: Lesson 3 recommends storytelling at every stage, such as tracing a jacket's wool back to the farm.
